posts.name: Windfox
posts.cooked:
If you just did the search currently as of today, it should have improved the results based on user feedback. As long as we’re giving valid corrective search measures, the search field should theoretically narrow to desired results. Rufus will ask, “Is this what you’re looking for?” and then keep stripping products from the search list until it gets a correct response.

I was searching for the lemon juicer in July. There’s been 5-ish months for my and other users feedback to recalibrate the results. A lemon juicer isn’t a super sought after, popular buy item that gets a lot of input. You usually happen to buy perhaps one, maybe two in a lifetime. Mine just happened to break after 25 years of use, so I needed another. Since it’s not popular, but actual bullet juicers are (and their motors seem to kick the bucket every 3-4 years) it makes sense they were at the top of the list to start with. The AI was making a best guess after products related to juicing in general.
